fields.meta_title: Tour Booking Form Builder With Seat Limits | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a tour booking form that closes full departures, sends large groups to the owner, and emails drivers their pickup list. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Tour Booking Form That Closes Each Departure When Full
fields.hero_description: Build a tour booking form that offers only departures with open seats and saves every booking to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What a Departure Needs Before Guests Arrive
fields.features_subheading: A tour booking form that counts seats on every departure, routes big groups, and tells each guide who is coming tomorrow.
fields.feature_1:
Departures that close when they fill

Set a seat cap for each departure time. Once the last seat is booked, that time drops off the form, and the next guest only sees walks with room for their whole party.
fields.feature_2:
Group size decides the next step

Bookings up to the size you set confirm on the spot. Anything larger goes to the owner by email with the date and the headcount, so a private price can go back that day.
fields.feature_3:
Pickups chosen from the stops you run

Guests pick a hotel or meeting point from a fixed list instead of typing an address. Each stop carries its own pickup time, and the confirmation email repeats it to the guest.
fields.feature_4:
A list for the guide the night before

At an hour you choose, the app emails each guide the next day's guests, party sizes, and pickup stops in order. Nobody has to export a spreadsheet before the morning run.
fields.feature_5:
Cancel a departure in one place

Mark a departure canceled on the dashboard when the weather turns or a guide calls in sick. The app emails every guest booked on it a link to a date that still has seats.
fields.feature_6:
Your booking app, exported to GitHub

On paid plans, export the full codebase to your GitHub repository. Run the booking app on your own hosting next to the tour site you already have, and keep building on it.
fields.why_title: Why Build Tour Booking Forms With Emergent?

fields.usecase_heading: How Four Tour Operators Take Bookings
fields.tab_content_1:
With 3 seats left, Delphine fills the 11:00 am walk

Saltgrass Food Walks caps every walk at 12 guests. Delphine Marchetti picks the Saturday 11:00 am walk, enters her name and email, and books 3 seats, the last 3 left. Her booking saves to the database, and the form takes the 11:00 am walk off the list for the next guest.
fields.tab_content_2:
For groups over 10, Anselm writes the quote

Cobblevine Bike Tours quotes large groups by hand, so any request for more than 10 riders goes to the owner, Anselm Ruiz, by email instead of confirming. Tallowmere Design asks for 16 riders on the vineyard loop for a company outing. Anselm sends a price that afternoon, while 4 smaller bookings confirm on their own.
fields.tab_content_3:
The driver gets all 18 pickups at 6:00 pm

Each Pinewater Coach Tours guest picks a pickup hotel from the 5 on the route, and each hotel has a set time. At 6:00 pm the night before, the app emails driver Benedikt Szabo the morning's list: 18 guests across 5 hotels, in stop order, starting at the Harborline Inn at 7:10 am.
fields.tab_content_4:
All 5 bookings on the canceled sailing get a link

Wind picked up over the harbor at 4:00 pm, and Captain Ines Halloran canceled the 6:30 pm Gullhaven Sunset Cruises sailing from the dashboard. The app emailed all 5 bookings, 14 guests in total, a link to choose another evening with open seats. Within the hour, 3 of the 5 had rebooked.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Tour Booking Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to plan the seats and pickups on a tour booking form, build it with Emergent, and test it from a phone.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Count the seats each guide can lead
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 List every departure for the season
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Ask only what the day needs
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Set a size for custom quotes
fields.howto_step_1_des: Count how many guests one guide can lead on each tour, then make that the seat cap for its departures. A walk down narrow streets and a 50-seat coach need different numbers. Set the cap tour by tour.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Write down each day and start time a tour runs this season. Guests can pick only these times. Take a holiday or a guide's day off out of the schedule before booking opens, not after someone books it.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Keep the form to what the guide uses on the day itself: the guest's name, email, departure, and party size. Add a pickup hotel only for tours that collect guests, and save directions and what to bring for the confirmation email.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Pick the party size above which you would rather quote by hand. Requests over that size skip instant confirmation and go to the owner. Write the number into the prompt so the form and the email use the same one.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Put the tours, seat caps, departures, and group rule into one prompt. Emergent builds the tour booking form, the database of bookings, and a dashboard that shows every departure. Ask in plain English when a tour or a start time changes.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Choose the hour each guide receives the next day's list and what it shows, such as each party's size and its hotel. Pick an hour late enough that a booking made after dinner still makes the list for the morning.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Book a test seat on your phone
fields.howto_step_7_des: Book the last open seat on a test departure from your phone. Check that the departure leaves the form, that the booking shows up on the dashboard, and that the confirmation email arrives with the right meeting point.

faq_plan.q: What is a tour booking form?
faq_plan.a: A tour booking form is the page where a guest reserves a place on a guided tour. It records the tour, the departure, the party size, and how to reach the guest, and each booking counts against the seats on that departure.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a tour booking form?
faq_plan.a: Write down your tours with the seat cap on each departure, then describe them in one prompt to Emergent's AI form builder. It builds the form and the database behind it, plus a dashboard of departures. Change a tour or a time later by asking in plain English.

faq_plan.q: How do I adapt a tour booking form template to my tours?
faq_plan.a: Set a seat cap on each departure first, then swap the template's open date picker for your real start times. Cut any question your guides never use on the day. Emergent can also build the form from a description of your own tours, with no response caps.

faq_plan.q: Can a tour booking form handle several departures on the same day?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Treat each start time as its own departure with its own seat count. A 10:00 am walk and a 2:00 pm walk then fill separately. A one-off date with a single start time, such as a gala or a workshop, fits an event booking form better.

faq_plan.q: What questions should a tour booking form ask?
faq_plan.a: Four answers run a tour: the departure, the number of guests, and the lead guest's name and email. Ask for the departure first. The form can then check seats before the guest types anything else. Any extra question, like a pickup hotel, should change something on the day of the tour.

faq_plan.q: How do I keep a tour booking form from overbooking a departure?
faq_plan.a: Count seats per departure, not per day. Give each departure a cap, and have the form compare the party size with the seats still open before it accepts a booking. A party of 4 then sees only the times with at least 4 seats open.

faq_plan.q: Can a tour booking form collect a hotel pickup for each guest?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Give guests a fixed list of the hotels you stop at, each with its own pickup time, rather than a free-text address box. That keeps the driver's list in stop order. Guests reserving the room itself need a hotel booking form, which is a different job.

faq_plan.q: How should a tour booking form handle private groups?
faq_plan.a: Set a party size above which a booking becomes a request instead of a confirmed seat. Send that request to whoever prices private tours, along with the group size and the date they want. The app can alert that person by email or in Slack when the request comes in.

faq_plan.q: What should a tour booking form send guests after they book?
faq_plan.a: Send a confirmation email with the tour, the start time, the party size, and the meeting point or pickup time. Add what to bring and how to reach the guide on the day. With Emergent, every booking lives in a database you own, and a later change updates one record.

faq_plan.q: Can a tour booking form take bookings for private charters?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Add a charter option that asks for the date and the group size, and route it to the owner instead of the public schedule. If the party also wants music on board, a dj booking form takes that request apart from the charter itself.
